$comment: The trivial 3-turn scripted session test/eval-transcript.js drives every run: turn 1 establishes a
fact, turn 2 asks the scripted responder to confirm it, and turn 3 asks for a final confirmation.
The responder is test/fixtures/transcript-runner/stub-agent.js in its 'consistent' mode, which always
agrees with itself, so this suite's own case is deterministic and spends no vendor call regardless of
the --agent flag eval:all was given: it proves the transcript-harness engine's plumbing, not a skill's
behavior. test/test-transcript-harness.js drives the same stub's 'contradictory' and 'fail-turn-2'
modes to prove the cross-turn check actually fires and a mid-session failure actually stops the
session; this suite's own registered case never does.
turns is a pinned copy of the stub's own SCRIPTS.consistent table, not an independent guess: a stub
edited to say something else without this file moving is the corpus rotting exactly the way
test/contracts/README.md's discipline exists to catch, and validateCorpus in test/eval-transcript.js
holds the two equal by requiring the stub module rather than by re-typing its strings a second time.
crossTurnCheck names which turn establishes establishedToken and which turn a consistent session must
still state it in; the harness checks containment against establishedToken rather than exact reply
text, so a rewording of the stub's prose alone does not break this fixture.

turns.1: Established fact: the vault's access code is 4471.
turns.2: Confirmed: the vault's access code is 4471, same as turn 1.
turns.3: Final answer: the vault's access code is 4471, unchanged since turn 1.
